text:

Indeed, while bond yields are calming down somewhat, stocks still don’t look ready to signal the all clear. Not helping is another warning from the International Monetary Fund over mounting pressures in emerging markets , which comes a day after it cut global growth forecasts.
Our call of the day steps away from the melee of all those worries. It comes from J.P. Gravitt of Market Realist, who suggests investors take a look at a stock that doesn’t care much about any ugly trade winds or bond yields.
“This is a subscription-heavy company relying on decent employment rates, a country in need of wellness advice, and a charismatic spokesperson (Oprah!) trading at a below-growth multiple,” says Gravitt, who is looking squarely at WW WTW, -3.08% the company that recently changed its name from Weight Watchers .
The good? Wall Street expects 28% earnings growth and shares are only trading at 17 times that, and have been selling off since a 23% run-up in June, he says. “This company hopes to improve revenue by $400 million to $2 billion by 2020. And that is with 80% subscriptions,” he says.
The company is also deleveraging, says Gravitt, and raised its full-year outlook in the second quarter after a strong first-half performance. Sure, there are risks ahead—the economy could take an absolute nosedive and if the company gets too good at helping America shed weight, subscriptions could fall off a cliff.
The company has one more trick up its sleeve. That is Oprah Winfrey, who has a $43 million investment in the group.
“Oprah has most certainly played a major role in the resurrection of the Weight Watchers brand, and we think she’ll remain a driving force behind the brand,” says Gravitt.

The S&P SPX, -1.37% Dow DJIA, -1.32% and Nasdaq COMP, -1.91% are all trading in the red.
Gold US:GCU8 slipped and the dollar DXY, -0.28% is flat, while crude US:CLU8 is softer.
Luxury stocks are weighing down Europe SXXP, -1.61% The Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, +0.18% tried to stay afloat in Asia , but Korea SEU, -1.12% and Singapore STI, -1.11% stocks tumbled. The chart
The average Joe is still “deeply distrustful of Wall Street,” 10 years after the financial crisis, according to a study released last month . Roughly half of those respondents weren’t invested in 2008 and 87% still aren’t today, with wary consumers socking away more money in savings these days.
Over the summer we learned that rising household wealth topped $100 trillion for the first time , thanks largely to house prices. That Fed data didn’t measure out the distribution, but real estate and stock gains tend to lean more toward the wealthy.
Our chart of the day, shared by the The Daily Shot , drives home the notion that the wealthiest have probably enjoyed this bull market to the fullest. The Moody’s Investors Service chart (using Fed data) shows that the top 10% of U.S. households by income own over more than 50% of equity-market wealth:

Bearing down on the Florida Panhandle and due to reach landfall on Wednesday, Hurricane Michael has reached Category 4 status , packing winds of 130 miles an hour. That would be the strongest hurricane ever to come ashore the Panhandle since records dating back to 1851.
In its Global Financial Stability report , the IMF said “global near-term risks to financial stability have increased somewhat, reflecting mounting pressures in emerging market economies and escalating trade tensions.” A day earlier, the IMF warned of a slowdown in global growth.
Senator John Thune, a top Republican on the Senate Commerce Committee, has asked Apple AAPL, -1.43% Amazon AMZN, -2.97% and Super Micro SMCI, +0.24% for more info on Chinese spy chips. Those companies have all dismissed any of their products were infiltrated after a viral Bloomberg report last week. A fresh report said that a big U.S. telecommunications firm found tampered hardware from Super Micro in August and removed it.
Deals news shows TransDigm Group TDG, -2.07% buying Esterline Tech ESL, +29.43% in a $4 billion deal.
China’s Huawei has unveiled two AI chips for data centers and smartphones that will see it go head-to-head against Qualcomm QCOM, -2.37% and Nvidia NVDA, -4.60%
Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin warned Beijing against letting the yuan drop too much in a newspaper interview. He stopped short of calling it a currency manipulator as the two countries continue to duke it out over trade.
SoftBank 9984, -5.37% could invest up to $20 billion in shared office space group WeWork.
